article_draft.title: Winklevoss group files for Zcash ETF at 0.25% fee, ticker WINK proposed
article_draft.body:
Winklevoss Asset Services filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the SEC on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, to launch a spot Zcash ETF under the ticker WINK on Nasdaq, with a 0.25% sponsor fee and Gemini Trust Company as custodian, according to reporting from U.Today.
The filing marks a return to ETF infrastructure for the Winklevoss twins, who submitted the first-ever spot Bitcoin ETF application to the SEC in 2013. The new fund undercuts Grayscale's existing Zcash ETF, which Grayscale converted from a trust in August 2026, by charging a lower fee.
The fund will hold Zcash (ZEC) directly and pursue passive exposure to the asset's price movements without leverage or derivatives, per U.Today's reporting. All ZEC owned by the trust will be stored by Gemini Trust Company, a New York State chartered limited liability trust company regulated by the New York State Department of Financial Services, in cold storage. Gemini is co-founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss and is an affiliate of the fund sponsor.
If approved, shares will trade on Nasdaq under the proposed WINK ticker. The fund will not attempt to produce any returns other than those that follow from ZEC's price movements, allowing investors to gain exposure to the cryptocurrency through regular brokerage accounts, according to U.Today.
Winklevoss Capital Fund has expressed an interest in purchasing up to $100 million worth of shares, though U.Today reports the prospective purchase is not a binding commitment. The filing tapped Cypherpunk Technologies, a Winklevoss-backed Zcash treasury company, as the fund's "Zcash Ecosystem Partner" to advise on protocol matters and coin holder voting, according to Decrypt.
Zcash is a privacy coin that lets users shield the sender, recipient, and amount of a transaction using cryptography called zk-SNARKs. Per Decrypt, the asset has surged over 2,000% in the last year and has climbed into the top ranks of digital assets after years as a regulatory pariah. Tyler Winklevoss publicly expressed excitement about Zcash last week, telling the industry that the momentum reminded him of 2019, per U.Today.
Competition in the Zcash ETF space is already present. Grayscale converted its Zcash Trust into a spot ETF in August and later moved to split its shares, while 21Shares listed Europe's first Zcash exchange-traded product. The SEC must still approve the Winklevoss filing before trading can begin.    Winklevoss Capital's $100 million share purchase is non-binding, signaling limited internal commitment.
article_draft.bottom_line: The SEC approval timeline for the Winklevoss Zcash ETF remains unconfirmed. Watch whether regulators signal concern over privacy coin exposure in institutional products, or whether the Glamsterdam upgrade and institutional adoption trends that followed BlackRock's tokenized fund initiative persuade the agency that regulated infrastructure for privacy assets can coexist with compliance frameworks.

article_draft.title: Ethereum's Glamsterdam test gets last-minute fix before gas-capacity jump on Sepolia
article_draft.body:
One of Ethereum's main validator clients released a software update hours before the Sepolia testnet activated the Glamsterdam upgrade on October 6, 2026, according to CoinDesk. The upgrade raises the amount of work each block can hold to 200 million gas, a significant increase from the current 60 million.

Epochs finalized smoothly on the testnet following activation, with early blocks beginning a gradual climb toward the 200 million gas-limit target, per The Defiant. The upgrade compresses a major scalability milestone into a single coordinated client release, a pattern Ethereum has followed for previous network changes.

The timing of the last-minute client update underscores the precision required to execute protocol changes across a decentralized validator set. Ethereum's testnets serve as proving grounds before mainnet activation, allowing developers to observe how the network handles changes in real conditions without production risk.
article_draft.bottom_line: CoinDesk and The Defiant do not specify which client released the update or what specific issue it addressed. Readers should monitor Ethereum's core developer channels and the foundation's official upgrade posts for details on the fix and the timeline for Glamsterdam mainnet activation.

article_draft.title: Solana Foundation launches open-source settlement program with JPMorgan's input
article_draft.body:
Solana Foundation launched Solana DvP, an open-source escrow program released under the permissive MIT license that gives financial institutions a standardized API for delivery-versus-payment settlement on the Solana blockchain, according to Decrypt. JPMorgan provided input on institutional settlement practices that shaped the design.
Delivery-versus-payment, or DvP, is a settlement mechanism that ensures both legs of a trade occur simultaneously, reducing counterparty risk. In conventional markets, DvP runs through a multi-day chain of clearinghouses, depositories, and custodians that can lock up capital for a day or two, per Decrypt. Solana DvP compresses settlement into a single atomic transaction, where both legs settle together or neither does.
Catherine Gu, the Solana Foundation's head of product for digital assets, said the program offers institutions a single open standard "with finality in seconds instead of days," according to Decrypt. Gu added that atomic settlement removes counterparty risk inherent in traditional finance.
Rhodel D'Souza, J.P. Morgan's head of markets digital assets, said a shared, open standard for atomic delivery-versus-payment is "exactly the kind of foundational infrastructure institutional market participants require," per Decrypt.
Solana DvP supports SPL Token and Token-2022, including extensions regulated issuers depend on such as permanent delegate, pausable tokens, and transfer hooks, per Decrypt.  The foundation said it plans to add privacy features so settlements can be kept confidential, per Decrypt.
Solana has emerged as a leading venue for tokenized equities and institutional products. BlackRock launched a tokenized money market fund for stablecoin reserves that records ownership on Solana alongside Ethereum in August, and the fund was structured to qualify as a reserve asset under the GENIUS Act, per Decrypt. Kraken has used Solana to offer tokenized U.S. stocks to overseas customers through its xStocks product, per Decrypt.
article_draft.bottom_line: The identity of the external auditors and their audit findings remain unreported. Watch whether the Solana Foundation publishes audit reports and whether major custody providers, broker-dealers, or asset managers announce integration with Solana DvP in production over the next quarter.
